svg.title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scale
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-four-core-six-scaled-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scale; subtitle: 2 FT + 2 C core pod; add 1 FT + 1 C for a 3 FT + 3 C scaled pod.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Numeric values show core-seat occupancy: four values of one and two expansion values of zero. The core comprises 2 FT + 2 C; activating both expansion seats produces 3 FT + 3 C, six people total. Contractor seats represent individual capacity commitments, not guaranteed full-time employee equivalents. External vendor and trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount.; caption: Conservative and Base scenarios use the four-person core; the Scaled scenario uses all six seats. Consolidate operating responsibilities within the core before expansion, and verify worker classification from actual working arrangements.; stages: label: FT 1: Owner-manager and estimator; value: Core employee seat; commercial and scope accountability; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own pricing, cash forecasting, jurisdiction selection, Xactimate estimates, measured quantities, and supplement support. Escalate contractual disputes appropriately without negotiating policy coverage or claim settlement.; label: FT 2: Project and mitigation lead; value: Core employee seat; field delivery, safety, and quality; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Coordinate dispatch and trades, direct extraction and drying, verify psychrometric records and hazard controls, review job costs, and confirm completion before billing. Maintain required qualifications for assigned work.; label: C 1: Mitigation technician; value: Core contractor seat; extraction and monitoring capacity; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Perform agreed extraction, equipment handling, moisture monitoring, and containment tasks within documented qualifications and the project's hazard-control plan. Record equipment checks and removal evidence.; label: C 2: Dispatch and receivables coordinator; value: Core contractor seat; scheduling and billing support; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Coordinate arrivals, maintain authorization records, prepare invoices, track aging, and reconcile cleared payments under the agreed service scope. The owner-manager retains commercial accountability and approval authority.; label: FT 3: Safety and quality lead; value: Expansion employee seat; core occupancy zero; numeric value: 0.0; detail: Activate at scale to audit hazard controls, training, field records, and rework. The project and mitigation lead retains these responsibilities before this hire.; label: C 3: Reconstruction coordinator; value: Expansion contractor seat; core occupancy zero; numeric value: 0.0; detail: Activate at scale to coordinate qualified trade vendors, approved repair scopes, moisture acceptance criteria, and completion records. External trade sub-crews remain direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not pod seats.
